scope: Theorem 3.1 (The resolvent expansion and double-layer positivity) of the manuscript “A direct proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality” (preprints/A-direct-proof-of-the-complete-Crouzeix-inequality-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 325 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d9aa4ef2dccb1f04), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Ω, h, q, and (bk) satisfy the hypotheses and conclusions of Theorem 2.1. For any positive integer n and A ∈ Mn(C) with W(A) ⊂ Ω, on T let R(λ) = q(λ)(h(λ)I − A)−1 . (3.1) Then R(λ) = X k≥0 bk(A)λ−k , R(λ) + R(λ)∗ ⪰ 0. For the fixed A, h, there are constants C < ∞ and 0 < θ < 1 such that ∥bk(A)∥ ≤ Cθk for all k ≥ 0. Thus the series converges absolutely and uniformly on T. In particular, R T R dτ = I and R T(R + R∗) dτ = 2I.
